CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFOUTPUT

CFOUTPUT is the tag that turns #Variable# into text. Inside its body every expression between pound signs is evaluated and written to the page. Give it a QUERY attribute and the body is repeated once for each row of the query; add GROUP and you get one pass per group of rows, with nested CFOUTPUT tags walking the rows inside each group.

Category

Output and page processing

Syntax

<CFOUTPUT QUERY="query_name"
    GROUP="column[,column]"
    GROUPCASESENSITIVE="Yes/No"
    STARTROW="start_row"
    MAXROWS="max_rows_output">
  Literal text, HTML and #expressions#
</CFOUTPUT>

Attributes

QUERY
Optional. Name of the query to loop over. Inside the body, columns of the current row can be written without the query prefix (#LastName#), and query_name.CurrentRow tells you where you are.
GROUP
Optional. Column (or comma-separated list of columns) that defines a group. The body runs once for each run of consecutive rows with the same value, so the query should be sorted by that column with ORDER BY. Nested CFOUTPUT tags without a QUERY attribute output the rows (or sub-groups) of the current group.
GROUPCASESENSITIVE
Optional, default "Yes". Whether grouping compares values case-sensitively. With "No", "Apple" and "APPLE" fall into the same group.
STARTROW
Optional, default "1". First row of the query to output.
MAXROWS
Optional. Maximum number of rows (or, with GROUP, groups) to output.

Usage

Outside a CFOUTPUT block, pound signs are just pound signs. Inside one, write ## to get a literal #, which matters for HTML colors: <TD BGCOLOR="##CCCCFF">.

Grouping works on consecutive rows only. Sort the query by the group columns (ORDER BY Region, State) or the same group will show up more than once. You can nest as many grouped levels as there are GROUP columns; the innermost CFOUTPUT without GROUP prints the detail rows. Only the outermost tag may name the query: a query-driven CFOUTPUT inside another query-driven CFOUTPUT raises "Invalid tag nesting configuration".

STARTROW and MAXROWS are the classic building blocks of "next 10 records" pages. Use CFLOOP with QUERY when you want to loop over a second query inside an output block, and CFSETTING ENABLECFOUTPUTONLY when you want everything outside CFOUTPUT to be silent.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- One pass per region, one line per state, every park listed --->
<CFQUERY NAME="GetParks" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT ParkName, Region, State
FROM Parks
WHERE Region IN ('Southwest', 'Pacific West')
ORDER BY Region, State, ParkName
</CFQUERY>

<CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetParks" GROUP="Region">
  <H4>#Region#</H4>
  <UL>
  <CFOUTPUT GROUP="State">
    <LI><B>#State#</B>:
    <CFOUTPUT>&middot; #ParkName# </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  </UL>
</CFOUTPUT>

<H4>Rows 3 and 4 only (STARTROW="3" MAXROWS="2")</H4>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetParks" STARTROW="3" MAXROWS="2">
  <TR><TD>#CurrentRow#</TD><TD>#ParkName#</TD><TD>#State#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
